UK to see rain and cooler conditions this week after fifth summer heatwave

The UK can expect fresher conditions this week, with rain and even thunderstorms possible in some parts of the country following weeks of hot and dry weather.

A Met Office meteorologist said that the south of the UK will experience “changeable” conditions as temperatures turn “cooler”.

However, a yellow heat health alert has been extended until 9am on Tuesday for the South East, South West, and London.

The UK recently experienced its fifth heatwave of the summer, with the hottest day of the year recorded in Kew Gardens, London, on Thursday, when temperatures reached 38.1C.

“I can’t promise rain for all of us through the week ahead, but in the south at least, it’s looking like the most changeable week we’ve seen here – well at least since the end of June," Met Office meteorologist Tom Morgan said on Sunday.

Showers are expected to become more widespread on Thursday with a mix of sunshine and rain earlier in the week, according to the Met Office.

South Wales Fire and Rescue Service said just before 7pm on Saturday that it was experiencing an “unprecedented demand”, having received 736 calls compared with an average of about 300.
